focus: Q11: outside the sk-code hub, inventory external tooling assumptions and the user-facing deletion path
noveltyJustification: Three newly located cross-cutting consumers were supported, while four findings add bounded checks or qualifications rather than a complete deletion test.
ruledOut: Treating the archived benchmark PASS as a deletion-test result: it records zero scored and eligible rows.
Treating advisor Obsidian/Webflow marker fixtures as dependencies on installed sk-code packets: the test seeds temporary workspaces.

label: The sk-code feature catalog calls the registered Webflow, OpenCode and Obsidian packets the current live surface inventory, so it becomes inaccurate after an external user removes the two examples.

The Webflow-plus-Motion manual scenario requires WEBFLOW and named sk-code-webflow references and assets in both its expected loads and pass criteria, so deletion makes that example-specific scenario un-runnable against the adapted tree.

The quality mode still routes Obsidian work to checklists under sk-code-obsidian and its frontend source list links through sk-code-webflow; removing either packet without updating these consumers leaves missing target-specific quality material.

The .opencode and .hermes sk-code mirrors still state that the hub has exactly three surfaces and list Webflow and Obsidian; a mirror not refreshed after canonical removal would continue advertising deleted paths. Mirror refresh was not tested.
An archived compiled-routing benchmark says PASS but has zero scored and eligible rows and routes its gold expectation to code-webflow; it is not evidence that an example-pruned tree passes.

Advisor surface-hint tests create Obsidian and Webflow markers in temporary workspaces and assert the hint value without relying on installed sk-code packet directories; retain these detector fixtures. The separate webflow cms scorer routes to mcp-code-mode, not sk-code.

Doctor check 3c emits the exact message that the registered packet is not an existing sub-directory, but the message contains no recovery action. This directly re-confirms round-one F33 from the implementation branch; it does not establish a new failure mode.

direction: Interpret the archived benchmark PASS as proof the example-pruned tree works
reason: The report records zero scored/eligible rows and its scenarios route to the code-webflow gold expectation.

direction: Remove advisor Obsidian/Webflow detection fixtures because the sk-code examples are optional
reason: The test creates marker files in isolated temporary workspaces and verifies surface hints without loading example packets.
